To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the correlation between BL Lacs, which have been selected by the UHECR arrival directions, and the UHECR directions itself is not significant, and the significance of the UHEC- BL Lacs correlation is intensively depending upon the GMF model used in the calculations of the deflections.
The significance of a correlation between the locations of BL Lacs and the arrival directions measured by AGASA depends on the galactic magnetic field model.
only a special GMF model, among all GMF models, can make the correlation between the locations of the BL Lacs and the arrival directions measured by AGASA significant.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the significance of the correlations between the UHEC and BL Lacs, but not the existence of the correlation itself.
the correlation between BL Lacs, the UHECR sources, and the arrival directions, and it is not concerned with the UHECR source origin.
the significance of correlation between BL Lacs with UHECRs by using different GMFs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no evidence for correlation between the UHCECRs and the BL Lacs.
there exists a weak correlation between the BL Lacs and the UHECR arrival directions, which may be due to a chance.
the correlation between the selected BL Lacertae objects and the arrival directions measured by the AGAS experiment is insignificant.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the correlation between BL Lacs (selected using a simple method) and the UHECR arrival directions, calculated using deflections of the particles with charge +1 and assuming the GMF models, is not significant.
the correlation between the BL Lacs and the UHECR arrival directions is not significant.
the correlation is still not significant enough to support the assumption of +1 charged UHECRs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the significance of correlation between BL Lacs, UHECRs deflected by using GMF models, and the UHECR arrival directions should be treated as a GMF model dependent quantity.
the significance of correlation between the UHCRs and BL Lacs depends on the GMF models and the statistics of the UHCR data.
the correlation between the arrival directions of UHECRs detected by the AGASA and the locations of BL Lacs is not significant.
